why: coarsen to all: SUM (additive)
examples.sql: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "festival_detail"."Festival_Name" AS g, COUNT(*) AS m1 FROM "nomination" JOIN "festival_detail" ON "festival_detail"."Festival_ID" = "nomination"."Festival_ID" GROUP BY "festival_detail"."Festival_Name") SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS m1 FROM "s1"
examples.instruction:
Step 1. Start from each `nomination` record; combine it with each `festival_detail` record for which Festival ID (`festival_detail.Festival_ID`) equals Festival ID (`nomination.Festival_ID`), one combined record per match (a record without a match is dropped); group the kept records by festival name (`festival_detail.Festival_Name`); each group gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) festival name (`festival_detail.Festival_Name`); (2) the number of records in the group.
Step 2 (the answer). Start from the rows of step 1; all kept records form one group, which gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) the sum of column (2) of step 1 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none).
